event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: KMB’s 2021-02-11 Form 10-K links the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic to both realized and forward-looking risks across supply chain, labour, demand patterns, cybersecurity and macro-economic volatility.  Because the filing date is within one year of the WHO pandemic declaration (March 2020), the Time Decay Principle allows high severity scores.  The document evidences concrete operational impacts already experienced in 2020 (e.g., +14 % tissue volume, −10 % K-C Professional volume, temporary plant closures, employee absences, FX and commodity swings) as well as explicit warnings of future uncertainties (duration, severity, consumer behaviour shifts, remote-work cyber exposure).  While several mitigating notes appear (e.g., facilities largely exempt from shutdowns, expectations of long-term positioning), these do not materially offset the breadth and immediacy of the risks.  Overall, the disclosures represent high-impact, recent, partly quantified evidence deserving upper-tier scores (7-9) with slight reductions where language is generic or contains stated mitigations.

evidence_list.snippet: We face various risks related to health epidemics, pandemics and similar outbreaks, which may have material adverse effects on our business, financial position, results of operations and cash flows.

components.reason: Explicitly acknowledges pandemics as a material adverse risk.
Generic wording without COVID-19 specifics.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Clear statement of potential material harm, but generic phrasing keeps score moderate.

evidence_list.snippet: The ongoing COVID-19 pandemic could have negative impacts on our business, including causing significant volatility in demand for our products, changes in consumer behavior and preference, disruptions in our manufacturing and supply chain operations, disruptions to our cost saving programs and restructuring initiatives, limitations on our employees’ ability to work and travel, significant changes in the economic or political conditions in markets in which we operate and related currency and commodity volatility.

components.reason: Specifies multiple operational and financial impact channels tied directly to COVID-19.
Uses strong language ('significant volatility', 'disruptions').
Forward-looking conditional ('could') rather than realised numbers.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Rich enumeration of concrete pandemic threats drives a high score despite forward-looking modality.

evidence_list.snippet: Despite our efforts to manage these impacts, their ultimate impact also depends on factors beyond our knowledge or control, including the duration and severity of any such outbreak and actions taken to contain its spread and mitigate its public health effects.

components.reason: Highlights uncontrollable uncertainty about duration/severity.
Contains mitigating language about management efforts.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Acknowledges unpredictable risk but simultaneously references mitigation, yielding a low-moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: The risk of cyber-based attacks is heightened with many of our employees working and accessing our technology infrastructure remotely as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Connects pandemic-driven remote work to increased cybersecurity risk.
Specific causal linkage ('heightened') increases severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct causal link between COVID remote work and elevated cyber risk justifies an above-average score.

evidence_list.snippet: These activities are subject to inherent risks such as natural disasters, power outages, fires or explosions, labor strikes, terrorism, epidemics, pandemics (including the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic), import restrictions, regional economic, business, environmental or political events ... which could disrupt our supply chain and impair our ability to manufacture or sell our products.

components.reason: Explicitly lists COVID-19 as a disruption threat to supply chain and manufacturing.
Embedded in broader generic list, diluting specificity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Supply-chain disruption risk named but within a catch-all list, yielding a mid-level score.

evidence_list.snippet: We continue to actively address the COVID-19 situation and its impact globally.

components.reason: Confirms active engagement with pandemic impacts (ongoing relevance).
No detail on severity or financial magnitude.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Statement signals ongoing risk management but lacks detail; score is modest.

evidence_list.snippet: We believe that we will emerge from these events well positioned for long-term growth, though we cannot reasonably estimate the duration and severity of this global pandemic or its ultimate impact on the global economy and our business and results.

components.reason: Admits inability to estimate pandemic duration/severity—high uncertainty.
Expresses optimistic mitigation ('well positioned'),

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Uncertainty acknowledged but tempered by optimism; risk signal is mild.

evidence_list.snippet: We have experienced increased volatility in demand for some of our products as consumers adapt to the evolving environment.

components.reason: Reports actual demand volatility attributable to pandemic.
Lacks quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Realised impact elevates score despite absence of specific numbers.

evidence_list.snippet: Beginning in the first quarter of 2020, particularly in March, demand increased in our Consumer Tissue and Personal Care business segments across all major geographies as consumers increased home inventory levels in response to COVID-19.

components.reason: Specifies timing and segment-wide demand surge linked to COVID-19.
Implied operational strain but no financial figure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Detailed temporal linkage of demand spike earns solid mid-high score.

evidence_list.snippet: The increase was followed by a period of demand softness as consumers used existing home inventories and demand returned to more normal levels.

components.reason: Describes pandemic-induced demand whiplash (volatility).
Implies partial normalization (mitigation).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows volatility but also reversion, giving moderate risk weight.

evidence_list.snippet: Demand for our consumer tissue products was elevated throughout 2020 as more people spent more time at home.

components.reason: Confirms sustained, pandemic-related shift in demand.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Persistent demand change tied to pandemic merits mid-range score.

evidence_list.snippet: Our K-C Professional business experienced volume declines throughout 2020 reflecting the reduction in away from home demand.

components.reason: Reports actual volume decline in a segment due to pandemic behavioural shift.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Quantifies directional impact (decline) on specific segment—above-average score.

evidence_list.snippet: During 2020, we experienced temporary closures of certain facilities, though we did not experience a material impact from a plant closure and our facilities were largely exempt or partially exempt from government closure orders.

components.reason: Mentions operational disruption (plant closures).
States impact was not material and exemptions existed (mitigation).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Disruption disclosed but downplayed as immaterial, so score is low.

evidence_list.snippet: At many of our facilities, we have been experiencing increased employee absences, which may continue in the current situation.

components.reason: Identifies labour availability risk linked to pandemic.
Future uncertainty qualifier ('may continue').

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Labour risk is direct and ongoing, justifying strong score.

evidence_list.snippet: During 2020, we also experienced increased volatility in foreign currency exchange rates and commodity prices, as certain countries experienced increased macro-economic volatility from the COVID-19 situation.

components.reason: Connects pandemic to macro-economic/FX/commodity volatility.
Actual experience in 2020 (realised impact).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Realised financial market volatility attributed to COVID-19 drives high score.

evidence_list.snippet: Volume increased 14 percent reflecting strong demand related to the COVID-19 and work from home environment, along with improved performance in Kleenex facial tissue.

components.reason: Provides quantified (+14 %) impact directly linked to COVID-related behaviour.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete, quantified effect on volume supports high severity.

evidence_list.snippet: Volumes decreased 10 percent, reflecting lower away from home demand and challenging business conditions following the outbreak of COVID-19.

components.reason: Quantified (−10 %) negative impact due to COVID-19.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Material, numeric decline attributed to pandemic justifies very high score.

evidence_list.snippet: Volumes decreased by 17 percent, reflecting lower away from home demand and challenging business conditions following the outbreak of COVID-19 with declines in all major markets.

components.reason: Even larger quantified (−17 %) decline across all markets tied to COVID-19.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Severe, segment-wide contraction linked to pandemic reaches near-maximum score.

evidence_list.snippet: Volumes decreased 11 percent, reflecting lower away from home demand and challenging business conditions following the outbreak of COVID-19, primarily in Western and Central Europe.

components.reason: Double-digit quantified decline attributed to COVID-19 in specific region.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Significant quantified regional impact earns very high score.
